question: A voice assistant application requires the lowest possible response latency among current Claude models so that spoken exchanges feel natural and immediate. Which model tier has the fastest comparative latency?
options: A) Claude Haiku, since it is described as having the fastest comparative latency of the current model lineup
B) Claude Opus, since higher intelligence models always respond with lower latency under normal load
C) Claude Sonnet, since its balance of speed and intelligence makes it faster than any other current tier
D) All current Claude models share the same comparative latency, differing only in output quality
correct_answers: A) Claude Haiku, since it is described as having the fastest comparative latency of the current model lineup
explanations: Correct. In Anthropic's model comparison, Haiku is listed with the fastest comparative latency among the current-generation models.
Greater intelligence does not translate into lower latency; Opus is listed with moderate comparative latency, slower than both Sonnet and Haiku.
Sonnet is described as fast, but the comparison table ranks Haiku's comparative latency ahead of Sonnet's.
The models differ noticeably in comparative latency, not just in output quality, which is precisely why latency is one of the criteria for choosing among them.
